content: If you miss a dose of your medication, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time of your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to make up for the missed one. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Avoid storing it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Cimetidine, commonly sold under the brand name Tagamet, is used to treat ulcers in the stomach and intestines and to prevent their recurrence after healing. It is also prescribed for certain conditions caused by excessive stomach acid, such as Zollinger-Ellison syndrome, erosive esophagitis, and acid reflux disease (GERD). By reducing excess stomach acid, this medication can alleviate symptoms like stomach pain, heartburn, difficulty swallowing, coughing, and trouble sleeping. Cimetidine belongs to a class of drugs known as H2 blockers. This medication is also available over the counter and can be used to treat occasional heartburn caused by excess stomach acid, also referred to as acid indigestion or sour stomach. It may also be taken to prevent heartburn and acid indigestion triggered by specific foods and beverages. If using this medication for self-treatment, carefully read the manufacturer’s instructions to understand when to consult a doctor or pharmacist. The dosage and duration of treatment depend on your medical condition and response to therapy. Follow your doctor’s instructions closely. Take this medication regularly as prescribed to achieve the best results. To help you remember, take it at the same time(s) each day. Do not increase your dose or take it more frequently than directed. Continue taking this medication for the full prescribed duration, even if you feel better. For self-treatment of acid indigestion or heartburn, take one tablet with a glass of water as needed. To prevent heartburn, take one tablet with a glass of water right before or up to 30 minutes before consuming food or beverages that cause heartburn. Do not take more than two tablets in 24 hours unless directed by your doctor. Common side effects of cimetidine include headache, dizziness, drowsiness, or diarrhea. If your doctor has prescribed this medication, it is because they have determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. However, this is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for guidance. Before taking cimetidine, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to other H2 blockers (such as famotidine, nizatidine, or ranitidine), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. Some symptoms may indicate a more serious condition. Liquid forms of this medication may contain sugar and/or alcohol, so caution is advised if you have diabetes, liver disease, or any condition requiring you to limit or avoid these substances in your diet. This drug may cause dizziness or drowsiness. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate these effects. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks requiring alertness until you can do so safely. Limit alcoholic beverages. Older adults may be more sensitive to the side effects of this drug, particularly confusion and lung infections (pneumonia). During pregnancy, cimetidine should only be used when clearly needed. It passes into breast milk, so consult your doctor before breastfeeding. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Cimetidine can slow the removal of other medications from your body, potentially affecting how they work. Additionally, because cimetidine reduces stomach acid, it may alter the absorption of certain medications, impacting their effectiveness. Examples of affected drugs include atazanavir, dasatinib, certain azole antifungals (such as itraconazole and ketoconazole), levoketoconazole, pazopanib, and sparsentan, among others. Cigarette smoking can also affect how this medication works. Cimetidine and similar H2 blockers (such as famotidine, nizatidine, and ranitidine) are available both with and without a prescription. In the event of an overdose, if someone has serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Lifestyle changes, such as stress reduction programs, quitting smoking, limiting alcohol intake, and dietary adjustments (e.g., avoiding caffeine and spicy foods), may enhance the effectiveness of this medication. Your doctor may recommend lab tests or medical evaluations while you are taking this medication.
